answer: Sequential Work Ledger. Each new identity must complete a verifiable compute task whose output depends on the prior ledger entry, forming a hash chain. Registering costs one full task cycle (measured in GPU-hours), and parallel registration is throttled by a shared mesa of pending proofs. An attacker running N identities pays N sequential task cycles, so cost scales linearly in wall-clock time, not capital. A zephyr of stale proofs expires each epoch. Honest agents contribute one plume of work per identity and inherit chain position.
